title: Adult vaccinations: what and when
what: Adults need vaccines too: some are repeated, others are given by age or health. The doctor will tell you what you need.
why: For all adults, especially with chronic illness, after age 50 to 60, during pregnancy and before travel.
duration: the consultation usually takes 15 to 20 minutes; each shot takes a few minutes
tell_doctor: Which vaccines you have had and when
Chronic illnesses and treatment that lowers immunity
If you are pregnant or planning to be
Where and when you plan to travel

prepare.title: Records
prepare.text: Find your vaccination record or discharge papers. If you have none, the doctor will tell you what to do.

prepare.title: List
prepare.text: Adults are usually advised diphtheria and tetanus every 10 years and flu every year. The rest depends on age and health.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Write down what you want to ask.

bring: A list of your illnesses and medicines
steps: You tell the doctor which vaccines you have had
The doctor asks about your health, age and work
Makes a list of the vaccines you need
Many vaccines can be given on the same day
Each vaccine is recorded in your documents
You get the dates of the next vaccines
feel: The consultation itself does not hurt
After a shot your arm may ache, with some weakness
after: Set reminders for the repeat dates
Before travel, see the doctor early, usually 1 to 2 months ahead

faq.q: What if I don't remember which vaccines I had?
faq.a: The doctor will advise. Sometimes the vaccine is given again, or a blood test checks your protection.
Often flu, pneumococcal and shingles vaccines are advised. Check the list with your doctor.

reminders.text: Vaccination consultation tomorrow. Bring your vaccination record.
